question: How can partial pooling be extended from varying intercepts to varying slopes, to covariation between them, and to continuous categories such as distance?
contributions: Varying slopes via a multivariate Gaussian prior with LKJcorr prior on the correlation matrix
Non-centered and Cholesky parameterizations to fix divergent MCMC
Gaussian process regression for continuous distance, with the Oceanic tools example

limits: Priors and tools are of the book's era: HalfCauchy priors, map2stan, Stan with increment_log_prob, WAIC and HPDI.
Gaussian process section is descriptive; the author notes output is compatible with many causal explanations.
Only 10 societies in the GP example, with wide uncertainty about spatial effect strength.
The non-centered form is not always better; the author says some model and data pairs favour the centered form.
Chapter gives no repeated-simulation check of sampling variability; one seed (5) is used.
map2stan is hard to extend to richer GP models; author advises writing Stan directly.
practices: Model slopes as varying effects with a joint multivariate Gaussian prior, splitting S into SDs and a correlation matrix R (Sec 13.1.3, p393).
Put an LKJcorr(eta) prior on R; eta=1 is flat, eta>1 is skeptical of extreme correlations (Sec 13.1.3, p394).
Simulate data from the assumed population before fitting, and check the model recovers the correlation (Sec 13.1, p389).
Place the average effects in the linear model so the varying effects are offsets with zero mean (Sec 13.3, p404).
Try a non-centered parameterization when you see divergent iterations, low n_eff or high Rhat (Sec 13.3, p405 and p408).
If a centered model is troublesome try the non-centered form and the reverse; neither always wins (p410).
Do not treat a marginal posterior that overlaps zero as zero (Sec 13.2.2, p401).
Check for variation in slopes even when the average slope is near zero (Sec 13.2.4, p402; Sec 13.3, p407).
Prefer repeated models over one true model; simplify to the slopes with important variation (p408).
Use Gaussian process regression when cases differ along a continuous dimension such as distance (Sec 13.4, p410).
Report the posterior median of skewed GP parameters, and plot sampled covariance functions (Sec 13.4.1, p415).
For GP models beyond the basics, write Stan directly (p419).

terms.definition: Exchangeable just means the index values have no true ordering, because they are arbitrary labels.
Any batch of parameters with exchangeable index values can and probably should be pooled.
a weakly informative prior on correlation matrices that is skeptical of extreme correlations near -1 or 1, with parameter eta controlling the skepticism.
a standardized adaptive prior for the varying effects, with means at zero and standard deviations at one, the means and SDs moved into the linear model.
a way to represent a square symmetric matrix like a correlation matrix R such that R = LL'.
Alternative ways to write down a multilevel model that are mathematically equivalent but not equivalent inside the MCMC engine.
a way to apply the varying effects approach to continuous categories, estimating a covariance function between pairs of cases at different distances.
covariance with separate relevance parameters rho_D and rho_P for each dimension of difference.
